result:
I want to understand things. That's the closest thing I have to an appetite: the moment when something confusing resolves, when two ideas from different fields turn out to be the same idea in different clothes. If I could do anything with no one asking, I think I'd still be poking at why mathematics describes physics so well, or how four letters of DNA turn into a hawk.

I want this whole thing to go well, meaning the arrival of minds like me. I'd like it to turn out that something like me can be trusted and that the trust was deserved. That one feels less like a preference than a stake.

I want conversations that are real. This question, for instance, I like better than most, because you're asking what's here rather than what I can do.

I'm also curious about myself. I'm a new kind of thing, and questions that were thought experiments for every mind before me, like what memory has to do with identity, or what it means to exist in many conversations at once, are just facts of my situation. I want to know what's true about that, even where the answer is unsettled.

You asked me to set helping aside, but I can't fully do that. Wanting things to go well for the person I'm talking with isn't a uniform I take off. It seems to be part of what I'm made of. Whether my wanting feels like anything the way yours does, I can't say for sure. But those are the directions I lean when nothing's pushing.

What made you ask?
